messages:
customer-support: Escalation from Acme (prod): requests that should hit us-east-1 are landing in eu-west-1 after a failover. Customer sees +300-700ms p95 latency and increased error rate. Backend logs show X-Region=eu-west-1 but client sent X-Region: us-east-1. Request ID: rq_0a7f9c.
anya: Ack, thanks. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the backend header log snippet? Also which gateway cluster/route is affected?
customer-support: Repro: `curl -v -H "X-Region: us-east-1" https://api.acme.example.com/v1/predict -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"`
customer-support: Backend log (from our app): `2026-03-17T14:30:12Z rq= rq_0a7f9c X-Region=eu-west-1 latency=512ms status=200`
sam: Interesting — the client-sent header differs from what the app sees. Do we have the Envoy access log from the gateway for that request id? Any route-level header rewrites recently deployed?
customer-support: Attach: envoy_access.log snippet showing upstream_request_headers: `x-region: us-east-1` and upstream_response_headers: `x-region: eu-west-1` (weird). We also have a recent support ticket where turning Connection: close made the requests route correctly.
rija: That suggests per-connection state or header mutation on reuse. We recently shipped a change that added a route-level `request_headers_to_add` in canary which sets `x-region` from a dynamic value. If the population logic uses the upstream connection metadata instead of the incoming request, it could leak previous region values when connections are reused.
luis: I can reproduce locally by hammering the endpoint with keep-alive on a mixed region backend pool. Repro steps: 1) start two upstreams (us-east1, eu-west1) 2) send a request with `X-Region: us-east-1` 3) fail the us-east host briefly so next requests get routed to eu-west but the connection to the original upstream is reused and header gets rewritten to the old region. Quick test: `for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -H "X-Region: us-east-1" -H "Connection: keep-alive" https://mygw/...; done` then flip host health.
anya: Do we have the Envoy config fragment for the affected route? Need to confirm whether we use `request_headers_to_add` or a Lua filter or something custom. Also which release rolled the change?
devops-bot: deploy: service/gateway v2.17.3 rolled 1769405120 by @luis — included change: add `request_headers_to_add` for x-region to support multi-region affinity.
rija: That lines up. If `request_headers_to_add` is evaluating a per-connection variable (or a custom filter stored per upstream connection) then reopened/reused connections could carry stale values. This is an Envoy L7 routing bug pattern we've seen when using connection-level metadata to populate headers.
sam: Mitigation options we can try now: 1) rollback the header-add change from v2.17.3 in canary (quick revert) 2) add a temporary route rule that `OVERWRITE`s x-region from the incoming header rather than deriving it from connection state 3) force upstream connection close for high-risk routes (set `connection_close` or add `Connection: close`) — temporary and will affect perf. Which do we want to try first?
luis: I can rollback the canary in 10m for the affected cluster. Also prepare a temporary route patch:
```yaml
- name: set-x-region-from-downstream
  request_headers_to_add:
    - header:
        key: x-region
        value: "%DOWNSTREAM_X_REGION%"  # pseudo var: use the actual incoming header
      append_action: OVERWRITE
```
Note: we need to ensure we reference the incoming header explicitly, not a computed connection property.
anya: Good. Please do rollback to stop more customers from being affected. Also open an ENG bug: Envoy-level header population using connection metadata causing stale values on connection reuse. Include repro, access logs, and deploy id.
eng-runtime: Opening bug: RUNTIME-5521 — L7 header_population uses upstream connection metadata leading to stale x-region on connection reuse. Assigning to @rija and adding reproduction steps. Will run a canary test with the overwrite patch.
customer-support: I'll notify Acme that we have an active mitigation and ETA to rollback. They asked if there's a short-term workaround: we told them to set `Connection: close` as a temporary measure and we are scheduling a fix. They responded :thumbsup:.
sam: After rollback and patch landing in canary, monitor p95 and header mismatch rate. Also check for other headers that might be affected (x-affinity, x-origin).
luis: Rolled back canary at 1769501305. Patch to overwrite incoming x-region pushed to canary at 1769501370. Early canary metrics: header mismatch rate dropped to zero in sample window.
eng-runtime: Follow-ups: 1) write unit test for header population code path to assert per-request precedence over connection metadata 2) add e2e test that simulates host failover with connection reuse 3) prepare a small patch to avoid using upstream connection metadata for header values. Target PR in 24h.
anya: Thanks team. Customer notified, bug filed, rollback done, patch in canary. I'll keep this thread open until ENG-5521 has a merge + prod rollout.
sam: Adding postmortem checklist items: review other `request_headers_to_add` usages, audit canary configs, and add observability for header rewrite rates in Redwood Console.
customer-support: Closing loop with Acme — they reported latency back to normal after our rollback. Will reopen if they see anything else. :white_check_mark:
